mappings.note: sector area for a stated 60 degree angle; the reason offers only pi*r^2 and the student must see the theta/360 factor is missing, which is the LO-1 formula itself
area described by a minute hand in 35 minutes - the exact example C-7.3-LO-1 names; the work is converting elapsed time to a swept angle, which no other outcome mentions
sector area from a GIVEN arc length rather than an angle; still the arc-and-sector pair of LO-1, using A = lr/2
plain sector area for a 30 degree central angle
PERIMETER of a sector, so the two bounding radii must be added to the arc; the sector area is never asked for, which is what separates this from LO-1
definition of a secant; the only outcome that touches chord/segment vocabulary is LO-2. Genuinely poor fit - it is a Circles-chapter terminology item with no area work at all, see report
asks only for the PERIMETER of the shaded region, arc plus the two chords; no area is computed anywhere in the item
inverts the sector-area formula to recover the central angle x from a given fraction of the circle; same relation as LO-1, run backwards
sector area from arc length 12 and radius 6, the arc-sector link of LO-1
minor SEGMENT cut off by a chord subtending 90 degrees; sector minus triangle, which is LO-2 and not the plain sector of LO-1
given the sector PERIMETER, strip the two radii to recover the arc, then get the area: the item crosses from perimeter to area and needs both outcomes
arc length formula solved for the radius given a 60 degree angle; arc length is the object, so LO-1 rather than the perimeter outcome
shaded region is the sum of three 60 degree sectors; the equilateral triangle only supplies the central angle, nothing is subtracted, so this stays LO-1 and not the composite LO-3
rectangle less two circles cut from it: a composite of circles and a polygon
rectangle less a semicircle on one side; composite subtraction, no central angle in play
difference of circumference and radius: the circumference is the unknown and the whole item lives on the perimeter side
MAJOR sector for a 45 degree minor angle - still a sector for a given central angle, taken as 315 degrees; no chord, so not the segment outcome
perimeter of a shaded region made of two square sides and two semicircular arcs; area is never asked
revolutions of two wheels over the same distance: circumference is the operative quantity, so the perimeter outcome and not the swept-area outcome
asks for BOTH the sector area and the arc length for a 60 degree angle - the two halves of LO-1 in one item
annulus area for a road round a park, but the datum is the park's CIRCUMFERENCE, so the perimeter-to-radius step is needed before the composite
three tethered horses each sweep a sector on their rope, exactly the rotating-arm model of C-7.3-LO-1; the angle-sum trick replaces any single given angle, so LO-1 does not fit
region between two concentric arcs of the same 30 degree angle: a difference of two sectors, so composite LO-3 rather than a single sector
horse on a 21 m rope at a corner sweeps a quadrant; the grazing tether is the same swept-area model as a wiper arm
circumference exceeds diameter by a given amount; purely a perimeter relation, no area anywhere
